title: Convert more Glib gboolean to C99 bool

notes.body: This change is replacing some GLib API calls specified to use a gboolean with a C99 bool instead (like https://docs.gtk.org/glib/method.String.free.html for example). Are you sure this is good practice? I remember avoiding those on purpose when we started the conversion.
Indeed. `gboolean` != `bool`, for example on big endian systems this can lead to wrong behaviour of the Glib functions.
okej, I can restore that one, any more you saw?
To be honest I did not do a real review, just spotted this change and stopped here.

For epan/wslua/wslua_debugger.c

Must stay as GLib types (API contract):

- bp_site_key_hash signature → guint, gconstpointer (GHashFunc)
- bp_site_key_equal signature → gconstpointer (GEqualFunc)
- bp_site_key_free signature → gpointer (GDestroyNotify)
- g_array_new(FALSE, TRUE, ...) → GLib API takes gboolean
- g_string_free(..., TRUE/true) → GLib API takes gboolean
- g_atomic_pointer_set / gpointer variables → GLib atomic API
- gint breakpoint_state_dirty_atomic → used with g_atomic_int\_\*
- guint in for (guint i = 0; i \< variables_array-\>len; ...) → .len is guint

Debatable but should stay GLib (consistency with GLib casts):

- (guchar) casts for g_ascii_is\*() macros — these macros are GLib, and guchar is the idiomatic cast used with them
- (gsize) cast for g_strndup — GLib function taking gsize
- guint64 used with g_ascii_strtoull — returns guint64

Could safely convert to C99:

- unsigned h / (unsigned)k-\>line inside bp_site_key_hash — these are local variables, not part of the signature. However, since the function returns guint, keeping guint h is more consistent.

Verdict: Nothing in this file should be converted to C99.
